description: REQ-114's own THIRD kill-switch condition — the NEW absolute-dollar-loss signal this SAME revision adds to resolve iteration-7's FIND-602 — is defined with a STRICT greater-than comparison: `paused = true when ... (totalRecentDefaultLossUsd > RECENT_DEFAULT_LOSS_THRESHOLD_USD)` (behavioral-spec.md:924-927, mirrored verbatim in verification-architecture.md:29/133). `RECENT_DEFAULT_LOSS_THRESHOLD_USD` is DELIBERATELY set to `5.00` — the document's own text explains this choice as 'chosen here specifically so that ONE single bust-out default at REQ-105's own maximum possible loan size (`maxLoanUsd = $5.00`) is, BY ITSELF, already sufficient to trip this signal' (behavioral-spec.md:880-884). But because `maxLoanUsd` is ALSO exactly `$5.00` (REQ-105, line 743), a single bust-out default at the ladder's own maximum size produces `totalRecentDefaultLossUsd = 5.00` — which is NOT strictly greater than a threshold of `5.00`. Under the literal `>` comparison the requirement's own SHALL text specifies, this exact, headline scenario NEVER trips the absolute-loss branch: no single loan issued under this spec's own REQ-105 ladder can ever exceed `$5.00`, so the 'single max-size bust-out default trips it by itself' claim the threshold was explicitly chosen to satisfy is mathematically impossible to realize through this branch alone. The spec's own worked Edge Case at behavioral-spec.md:997-1004 makes this contradiction self-evident within the SAME document: it computes `totalRecentDefaultLossUsd = $5.00`, explicitly states this value 'EQUALS `RECENT_DEFAULT_LOSS_THRESHOLD_USD`' (line 1002), and then asserts `evaluateOverallDefaultKillSwitch` 'still returns `paused:true`' — a conclusion that directly contradicts the `>` operator defined seventy-five lines earlier in the SAME requirement. This is not a hypothetical concern: this is the PRIMARY, headline dilution-defeat proof obligation this SAME revision adds to close FIND-602 (PROP-114f, verification-architecture.md:137, and the identical fixture reproduced in behavioral-spec.md's own Acceptance Criteria at lines 1052-1060) — it asserts `evaluateOverallDefaultKillSwitch({..., totalRecentDefaultLossUsd:5.00}) === {paused:true}`, an outcome unachievable by any implementation that correctly follows the requirement's own literal `>` formula. Tellingly, the SAME document's OWN separate, later fixture isolating this third branch (behavioral-spec.md:1061-1066, `evaluateOverallDefaultKillSwitch({..., totalRecentDefaultLossUsd:5.01}) === {paused:true}`) deliberately uses `5.01` — ONE CENT ABOVE the threshold — showing the spec author elsewhere DOES treat the boundary as exclusive. The document therefore contains two internally-inconsistent fixtures for the exact same branch: one (PROP-114b's exhaustive-branch test) uses a value strictly above threshold to safely trip it; the other (PROP-114f, the fix's own headline proof obligation) uses a value exactly AT the threshold and expects the identical outcome. Because the ratio-based signal is precisely the one FIND-602 already proved CAN be diluted below `0.20` by co-existing healthy loan volume once `sampleSize >= 10`, and because this boundary bug means the absolute-loss signal can NEVER be tripped by a single loan at the ladder's own maximum size acting alone (it requires either multiple defaults summing above `$5.00`, or one default of more than `$5.00` — impossible under REQ-105's own `maxLoanUsd` cap), the EXACT scenario REQ-114's own rationale (behavioral-spec.md:807-838) was written to close — an established borrower defaulting on a single large loan at the ladder's own ceiling, while a maturing colony's other healthy loan volume dilutes the ratio below 0.20 — can, once again, slip through BOTH signals simultaneously in a colony whose bust-out default happens to land at exactly `$5.00` rather than some value strictly greater than it. This revision's own core fix for FIND-602 is therefore not genuinely resolved: it works for a default strictly larger than `$5.00` (impossible under this spec's own ladder cap) or for an accumulation of multiple smaller defaults summing past `$5.00`, but fails at exactly the single-largest-loan boundary the requirement's own rationale singles out as the headline case.

evidence.snippet: `RECENT_DEFAULT_LOSS_THRESHOLD_USD` defaults to `5.00` ... chosen here specifically so that ONE single bust-out default at REQ-105's own maximum possible loan size (`maxLoanUsd = $5.00`) is, BY ITSELF, already sufficient to trip this signal ... `paused = true` when ANY of THREE conditions hold ... OR (NEW this revision) `(totalRecentDefaultLossUsd > RECENT_DEFAULT_LOSS_THRESHOLD_USD)` ... `totalRecentDefaultLossUsd = $5.00`, which EQUALS `RECENT_DEFAULT_LOSS_THRESHOLD_USD` — `evaluateOverallDefaultKillSwitch` still returns `paused:true` ... [separately] `evaluateOverallDefaultKillSwitch({..., totalRecentDefaultLossUsd:5.01}) === {paused:true}`

crossCheck.note: The Pure-Core purity-map row for `evaluateOverallDefaultKillSwitch` (line 29) and PROP-114b (line 133) both restate the identical strict `(totalRecentDefaultLossUsd > RECENT_DEFAULT_LOSS_THRESHOLD_USD)` formula. PROP-114f (line 137) — the SPECIFIC proof obligation this revision adds to resolve FIND-602, described in its own row as 'the requirement's own core dilution-defeat proof' — requires the exact fixture that computes `totalRecentDefaultLossUsd:5.00` (equal to, not greater than, the `$5.00` threshold) and asserts `paused:true`. A correct implementation of the literal `>` formula stated in both this file and behavioral-spec.md would make PROP-114f's own bound fixture FAIL (return `paused:false` from the third branch, since the ratio branch is independently below 0.20 by this same fixture's own construction) — meaning this Tier-1 proof obligation, as currently specified, cannot be satisfied by any implementation that correctly follows the requirement's own SHALL text. Either the comparison operator must become `>=` (restoring the stated design intent that a single max-size default trips it 'by itself'), or PROP-114f's own fixture/expected-output must be corrected — but not both must be left as currently written, since they are mutually exclusive as stated.
